definitions.explanation: used with negative verbs to express strong denial or prohibition

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{絶対|ぜったい}に{来|く}ると{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think he will definitely come.

examples.japanese: この{試験|しけん}には{絶対|ぜったい}に{合格|ごうかく}したい。
examples.english: I absolutely want to pass this exam.

examples.japanese: {絶対|ぜったい}に{許|ゆる}さない。
ここでは{絶対|ぜったい}に{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}らないでください。
examples.english: Please absolutely do not take photos here.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{絶対|ぜったい}にそんなことを{言|い}わないと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think she would never say such a thing.

notes:
FORMATION:
{絶対|ぜったい} (absolute) + に (adverbializer)

USAGE PATTERNS:
- {絶対|ぜったい}に + affirmative → definitely, certainly
- {絶対|ぜったい}に + negative → never, absolutely not

INTENSITY:
One of the strongest emphatic adverbs in Japanese. Using it conveys very strong determination or prohibition.

CAUTION:
Overuse can sound dramatic or immature. In formal contexts, {必|かなら}ず (certainly) may be more appropriate for affirmative sentences.

COLLOCATIONS:
- {絶対|ぜったい}に{無理|むり} (absolutely impossible)
- {絶対|ぜったい}に{嫌|いや} (absolutely refuse)
- {絶対|ぜったい}に{間違|まちが}いない (definitely not wrong)
